label: Born in 1632
description: Christopher Wren was born in the same year as van Leeuwenhoek and Spinoza.

sources.quote: His son was born in 1632, as were van Leeuwenhoek and Spinoza.

label: Left Westminster School at age 15
description: Wren left Westminster School at fifteen and lived at Bletchington.

sources.quote: Scarburgh suggested that Wren should translate into Latin, the chapter in William Oughtred's Clavis Mathematicae on 'dialing', or the design of sun-dials.
At the age of fifteen years, Wren wrote to his father that he had been befriended by Scarburgh

label: Entered Wadham College
description: Wren entered Wadham College at the age of seventeen.

sources.quote: To return to Oxford we find Christopher Wren, at the age of seventeen, entering Wadham College.

label: Elected Fellow of All Souls
description: Wren was elected a Fellow of All Souls College in 1653.

sources.quote: The year 1653 saw the publishing of the first English edition of Harvey on the circulation, and found Wren a newly-elected Fellow of All Souls

label: Appointed Gresham Professor of Astronomy
description: Wren was transferred to London as Gresham Professor of Astronomy in 1657.

sources.quote: In 1657, the year of Harvey's death, Wren was being transferred to London as the youthful Gresham Professor of Astronomy.

label: Invented intravenous therapy
description: Wren made the great forward leap - the invention of intra-venous therapy, injecting substances into the bloodstream of animals.

sources.quote: Wren made the great forward leap - the invention of intra-venous therapy - which has so greatly changed contemporary practice.

label: Royal Society founded
description: Fourteen men met to form the Royal Society after Wren's lecture at Gresham College.

sources.quote: On 28 November 1660, after Wren's 'Wednesday lecture' at Gresham College, fourteen men, of whom a good proportion were physicians, met to form the Royal Society.

label: Appointed Savilian Professor of Astronomy
description: Wren was appointed Savilian Professor of Astronomy at Oxford in 1660.

sources.quote: In the same year Wren was appointed Savilian Professor of Astronomy at Oxford, succeeding his Wadham friend Seth Ward

label: Illustrated Cerebri Anatome
description: Wren drew the illustrations for Willis's book Cerebri Anatome in 1663.

sources.quote: During the spring of 1663 Wren drew the illustrations for much of Willis's great book Cerebri Anatome.

label: Designed Sheldonian Theatre
description: Wren was designing the Sheldonian Theatre at Oxford in 1663.

sources.quote: While Wren was designing the Sheldonian Theatre at Oxford in 1663 he was doubling as Willis's trusted dissector.

label: Contributed to Micrographia
description: Hooke acknowledged Wren as the first to attempt microscopic drawings in 1665.

sources.quote: We learn of the existence of this pioneer work by Wren through the quaint introduction to Micrographia written in 1665 by Robert Hooke

label: Sheldonian Theatre opened
description: The Sheldonian Theatre was opened in 1669.

sources.quote: at the opening of Wren's Sheldonian Theatre, in 1669

label: President of the Royal Society
description: Wren served as President of the Royal Society in the 1680s.

sources.quote: As late as 1682 we find Wren, when President of the Royal Society, commenting on communications concerning the anatomy of the eye

label: Died in ninety-first year
description: Wren lived into his ninety-first year.

sources.quote: he nevertheless lived into his ninety-first year
